writeup: TIC 150230753 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 16.45% and an orbital period of 4.668 days, though a data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the initially detected period of 2.3342 days represents only half the true orbital cycle. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 139.0, though the centroid offset of 2.3 arcseconds warrants attention. The detection achieves a strong BLS signal-to-noise of 235.7, and the candidate does not appear in six checked variable-star catalogs. The machine-learning screening score of 0.38 reflects moderate confidence that this represents a genuine astrophysical source rather than an instrumental artifact.
